sections.text: But the Great Souls, O Arjuna! Filled with My Divine Spirit, they worship Me, they fix their minds on Me and on Me alone, for they know that I am the imperishable Source of being.
Always extolling Me, strenuous, firm in their vows, prostrating themselves before Me, they worship Me continually with concentrated devotion.
Others worship Me with full consciousness as the One, the Manifold, the Omnipresent, the Universal.

We have been discussing chapter nine, Rajavidy Rajagohya Yoga. Yoga of Supreme Knowledge and Supreme Secret. So far we have seen the Bhagavan has revealed the supreme secret that I pervade everything in this Jagat.
And this Jagat is supported by my Maya, my association with Prakruti. Prakruti produces all that is moving and unmoving. But I am not in the Prakriti.
I am not in the beings in the Prakriti. Those beings are in me. I am not in the Jagat, but Jagat is in me.
In other words, my self supports the perception of the Jagat. So the Jagat exists as long as I perceive it. This world exists for me as long as I am conscious of it.
When Im not conscious of this Jagat, then this Jagat does not exist for me. The same way from the Supreme Consciousness. As long as that Supreme Consciousness is aware of the Jagat, that Jagat exists.
And therefore Bhagavan says that I am not in the Jagat, Jagat is in me. But then he also said that they are also not in me. The beings and things in this Jagat are also not in me.
In other words, the Jagat and the things and beings which I see in the Prakriti, they are not in the consciousness. The consciousness is not affected by this perceptions of the world outside. So Bhagawan created contradictory statements for us to understand.
Relationless relationship with Bhagavan. We are related to Bhagavan, as close to him as we are to our own selves. Because this world is created out of Bhagavans own self.
Therefore I cannot be further away from him than I am from my own self. And thats the secret which is the Supreme Secret. Even though I am as close to him as I am to my own self.
But I never feel his presence. So Bhagawan said, to feel my presence you have to identify with me. People who do not identify with me.
Bhagawan is explaining in last verse, 12 he says Moga Asa, Mogha Karmanaha, Moga Gnana Vicheta sah. This is the reason why we are not experiencing his presence. Because we are distracted by our vain desires.
Those desires prompt us to do vain actions. Because of our vain knowledge who we are, we consider this body, this mind, this intellect is to be me, this limited being to be me. Im driven by my Rajasic and Tamasic tendencies.
As we have seen, this Maya is the root cause of the production of this Jagat. Jagat comes into existence out of Maya. Maya has three qualities.
Sattva, Rajas and Tamas. Therefore everything in this Prakriti. Prakriti is nothing but the representation of Maya to us.
So everything in this Prakriti has those three qualities, Satvarajas and Dhammas. Awareness, activity and inertia. To exist in space and time, it has to have activity and inertia.
And Sattva is the awareness part of it. So everything in this Jagat has these three qualities. The permutation combination of these three qualities makes this plurality that we see like in a three color printing.
There are only three colors, but they create myriads of shades of color. We can create all kinds of pictures from the combination of those three colors. The same way, this Prakriti produces a variety of things and beings by permutation and combination of these three Gunas.
Bhagavan said that up to the level of human beings, people are just living by their instincts. All animals, plants, and aquatic life survive in the lap of Mother Nature. They are aware of their own existence.
But they are not aware of any other higher entity. Human beings are the only ones who have intellect. To realize that there got to be somebody higher than me, somebody greater than me to have the control over this world.
Having that understanding, I still dont identify with him, because Rajas and Tamas dominate. When Sattva is subdued by Rajas and Tamas, all my actions will be driven by those Rajasic and Tamasic tendencies. The Rajasic and Tamasic tendencies tell me that my happiness lies in this world out there.
Therefore all my efforts to achieve that happiness which is my true nature. Just like water seeks its own nature, happiness is our true nature. So we constantly seek bliss and happiness.
And therefore we work in the world outside. We never complain about why Im feeling good today. We always complain Im not feeling good.
Today because being good is my nature, being not feeling good is not my nature. Bhagavan said, you are not recognizing your nature because of your wrong knowledge about yourself. Mogha Gnana -- because of wrong knowledge, Vichetasaha -- my thinking is wrong about where my happiness lies.
Im working outside in a Rajasic manner to acquire things, to achieve things, to get happiness. Or I say, If I dont do anything, then Ill be happy -- thats the Tamasic tendency. Because of these two aspects of my nature, which are predominantly Rajasic and Tamasic, Im not identifying with him.
Bhagavan said that when he takes the human form, people do not recognize him and they avoid him, ignore him. We know everything about our own self and other beings, but we dont know about the divinity which is common in all of us -- the consciousness which is the common factor, the one thread which ties everything together in this universe. So therefore Bhagavan says Rakshasim Asuram Chaiva Prakritim Mohinim Shritaha -- by the nature of this Rajasic and Tamasic Prakriti, they are confused about their own self and about the divinity in all human beings.
In contrast, Mahatmanastumam Partha Devim Prakritim Ashritaha. In this path of evolution, everything evolves from Tamas to Sattva. Even in the evolution of our planet, we can see that first there was nothing but just inert matter.
Then came the organic life. Then gradually it evolved into more complex life, more intelligent life. So everything evolves from inertia to knowledge, from Tamas to Sattva.
Some are in the path of evolution at Tamasic level, but they are on the path of their own evolution. So next step is Rajas to be Rajasic. So in our self unfoldment, when you introspect and see what you find, if you find Tamasic quality, then replace it by Rajasic quality.
If you find Rajasic tendencies, replace them by Sattvic tendencies. So this is a conscious effort. As a human being, we have our freedom to choose how to behave.
So Bhagavan said, those Mahatmas who have evolved to Sattva, even Mahatma has Rajasic and Tamasic tendencies. But theyre subdued by Sattvic tendencies. In other cases, the Rajasic tendencies are subduing the Sattvic tendency.
Here the Sattvic tendencies are subduing the Rajasic and Tamasic tendencies. Devim Prakritim Ashritaha -- the Sattvic is considered the Devi, the divine quality, closer to reality. Bhajantim Ananya Manasaha -- knowing fully well that I am not this bundle of matter, not this mind, not this intellect.
Even though Im pulled by the tendencies of body, mind, and intellect. Im constantly reminding myself Im part of this all pervading consciousness. My consciousness is same as consciousness in all other being.
Bhajanti Ananya Manasa not having any other thought. Even though Im functioning in the world like everybody else. But that thought is constant in my mind that I am the divine being at the core of my being.
I am that supreme self, the all pervading consciousness. Knowing that Gnatva Bhuta dim avyam I am part of that immutable self which is all pervading. So we have discussed this example before.
The space in my car or my car is in this space. The car is in the space. Space is not in the car.
The space seems divided in different cars in different rooms. But it is not really divided. Otherwise the car cannot move in the space -- it would have Henrico space when it is in Henrico, Hanover space when its in Hanover County.
Gnatva Bhutadim Avyayam -- the self in me and the self in you are not two divided selves. The self in all beings is one. The consciousness which makes the entire Jagat possible is undivided.
Its not that my consciousness is different than your consciousness. Your equipment, my equipment are different. And therefore our manifest representations are different.
So Bhagavan says Mahatma. One who has evolved to that level of understanding that the self is undivided and all beings are existing in that consciousness. Bhajanti Ananyamanah he devotes himself to me without any other thought, constantly with a single pointed devotion.
There is no other doubt. There is no other identification. Even though he realizes that he is an individual functioning as this body, mind, intellect.
But that is only possible because the consciousness functioning. We know this body is inert because we have seen dead bodies. Dead body cannot function when the consciousness is not there.
Therefore we come to the conclusion that the body is inert. Body is nothing but made up of food which I have eaten all my life. But I am a conscious being.
Therefore my real identity is the consciousness and not this body. This Mahatma has come to this level of understanding. Therefore he is constantly devoting himself to that true self which is the consciousness.
Satatam, Kirta, Yanthamam, Yatantaschadravrataha. He is constantly doing kirtan to me. He is constantly praising me.
So we obviously kirtan, bhajan, kirtan. We hear these words in our day to day conversation. In our culture, bhajan is when we are thinking about the Lord; kirtan is when we are praising the Lord.
But here, the praise and thinking about the Lord carry a very different connotation. When I am praising the Lord, I am devoted to the Lord. Devotion is love for the Divine. Our love for the Divine becomes devotion, and love is nothing but identification.
When I identify with something or someone, I love that thing or that person. I love my BMW because I identify with my BMW. When I identify with the Lord as my Lord, then I devote myself to Him.
This devotion is nothing but my identification with the Lord. And therefore that kirtan -- kirtan is not that one Sunday afternoon or Saturday evening we get together, and, the noisy kirtan we do with equally noisy equipment. Kirtan is a constant thought in my mind that I am not this limited being, and my Lord is not divided into separate beings.
We all exist in his own being. We are only existing because he exists. I am only alive because the consciousness is functioning through me.
When the consciousness will not be there, I will be purely as just a bundle of matter. They will call it dead body and get rid of it as quickly as possible. Satatam Yatantascha Dridavrataha.
They are constantly striving, because they will be pulled by this Prakriti to identify with it -- to identify with my body, to go out and get things, to fall in love with things and beings outside. I have to constantly remind myself; therefore its Yatantaha. So once you get this knowledge from the books or from a guru, youre not done with it.
Thats just the beginning. Now you have to constantly remember it with everything you do. Constant efforts are required for even Mahatmas.
Dridavrataha -- they are steadfastly established in this knowledge. There is never a doubt that this is not true. Some of us read this, then read another book, and start doubting whether this is right or that is right.
One says there is Ishvara; another says there is no Ishvara. One path says there is no life after death.

The Mahatmas (great souls) are distinguished not by external achievements but by their inner orientation. They have taken refuge in the Daivi Prakriti - the divine nature of Sattva, truth, and awareness. While functioning in the world like everyone else, they maintain unwavering recognition that their true identity is not the body-mind but the all-pervading consciousness. Like the actor Amitabh Bachchan who never forgets he is Amitabh while playing a coolie, the Mahatma never loses awareness of the Self while playing worldly roles.
Bhajanti ananya manasah - they worship with single-pointed mind, with no other thought. This is not about excluding worldly duties, but about the constant background awareness that I am the divine being at the core of my existence. Such devotion is identification - the more you identify with something, the more you love it. The Mahatma identifies with the imperishable Self (bhutadim avyayam) that is the same in all beings. Just as the space in your car is not separate from space everywhere, consciousness in you is not separate from universal consciousness.
Krishna describes three approaches to this truth: seeing the Divine as One (ekatvena - Advaita), as separate Creator and creation (prthaktvena - Dvaita), or as present everywhere with many faces (bahudha vishvatomukham). Whatever your philosophical approach, if your goal is alignment with the Supreme, you will reach it. Practice this week: Whatever draws you spiritually - prayer, meditation, service, study - pursue it with drdha-vrata (firm resolve). The path matters less than the steadfastness with which you walk it.
